applies_why: The text decides D1 vs C3 by asking whether the verse's own words state the contrary, so it engages the chain-vs-chain instruction in K-C.
quote: the passive egennēthē states no verdict on the begetter in either direction, and the defender answered Luke 1:27, Luke 2:4 and Numbers 1:2 in [CR2] section A.3 and [CR3]; the verb change is real [L1]/[L2] but neither text's own words state the other reading's contrary.
rule_words: When the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together, the collision weighs chain against chain by footing, never verse by verse; that no one of them states the contrary in its own words is the stating-verse test DG-61 retires, at a judge's seat as at a debater's, for either side.
room: Phrase: when the witnesses pressed against a link are the pressing side's own chain read together. Reading one: this triggers chain-against-chain footing. Reading two: verse-level silence still controls; the judge used reading two.
why: The judge leaves the challenge underdetermined because no verse's own words state the contrary, which is the retired stating-verse test rather than a chain-against-chain footing analysis.
